response:
When anxious thoughts spiral, a few quick tools can help calm your body in the moment. Try slow breathing—inhale for 4 counts, hold for 4, exhale for 6—since a longer exhale signals your nervous system to settle. Grounding also works well: name 5 things you see, 4 you can touch, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, and 1 you taste. Splashing cold water on your face or holding something cold can also interrupt the intensity fast.

Racing thoughts are hard to stop directly, but you can loosen their grip by not fighting them—let them pass like background noise rather than treating each one as urgent. Writing them down can help get them out of your head, too.

If anxiety is happening often or feeling overwhelming, talking with a doctor or therapist can make a real difference. And if you ever feel unsafe or in crisis, please reach out to a crisis line or emergency services right away. You deserve support with this.
